newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary names APV board, says privatisation goes on.
newsitem.headline: Hungary names APV board, says privatisation goes on.

text.p: The Hungarian government, vowing its privatisation drive would continue, named officials to the state privatisation agency APV Rt on Thursday to replace members sacked in a scandal.

"The government is determined to continue the privatisation ...and considers irresponsible any calls for its suspensions or freezing," government spokesman Elemer Kiss told a news conference where he named the new officials.

Tamas Deutsch, a leader of the opposition Fidesz party and head of a special parliamentary commission investigating a scandal at APV over irregular payments of millions of dollars to a consultant, has called for suspension of privatisation until the end of the inquiry.

APV's board and the minister supervising privatisation were dismissed three weeks ago after publicity about irregular payments of 804 million forints in fees to consultant Marta Tocsik. Her contract had been awarded without competitive bidding.
Kiss said the new president of APV will be Arpad Kovacs. He said Pal Szabo would become general director as of November 1, replacing Istvan Kocsis who leaves at the end of this month.

Kiss said the new members of the board are Andras Bognar, Gyorgy Csaki, Rezso Harsfalvi, Imre Kocsis, Karoly Lovasz and Istvan Tompe. Another three board members were expected to be named by next Wednesday, pending a security screening.
He said "the government will respect (existing) privatisation agreements and contracts and has no intention of amending them."
